mintAuthority.summary: USDh's sole authored Stacks deployment is the canonical native-issuance route. Mints require a two-step backend attestation: a KYC-whitelisted minter calls request-mint and deposits BTC, then Hermetica's trader opens the delta-neutral hedge off-chain and calls confirm-mint to release USDh, making supply gated by Hermetica's off-chain operator. No bridge representation or bridge administrator is evidenced, so bridge machinery is outside Mint Authority. D14 review 2026-10-03 reuses pinned owner evidence at Stacks height 9106999 (index hash 0x6211b0574e113e7ae2cdb5d4c8bf08caec41aab7c9829483e20e2c8b214b5c36), which establishes the owner as 2-of-3. The owner can authorize a replacement minting contract after 1008 burn blocks rather than only increase deposit-backed OTC capacity; the current OTC window is not a hard economic supply bound. Economic semantics are unbounded with periodic reconciliation. Multisig/backend roots do not qualify for D29 token governance.

No permissionless mint path exists. controls.capDescription: minting-otc-v1-1 confirm-mint is bounded by a rolling mint-limit (live: 1,000,000 USDh per 1,200s window); set-mint-limit asserts new-limit <= the max-mint-limit constant (1,000,000 USDh), so the confirm-mint operators cannot raise the ceiling.

controls.label: Minter whitelist (KYC/KYB gate)
controls.evidence: Only KYC/KYB-approved participants whitelisted by Hermetica can request mints/redemptions directly; access to the mint route is administered off-chain by the issuer.
